sample_unit: standardized psychodermatology scenarios (each answered by 5 LLMs in English and Turkish, rated by 3 clinicians)

links.outcome: LLM response quality by language (English vs Turkish) across models
links.effect: LLaMA 3.1 showed significantly lower quality in Turkish (66.3%) than English (77.2%; P < 0.001); Gemini 2.5 Flash scored highest in both languages.
links.quote: LLaMA 3.1 showed significantly lower quality in Turkish (66.3%) compared with English (77.2%; P < 0.001).

links.outcome: Risk management and actionability scores of LLM patient-facing responses
links.effect: Across models, actionability and risk management scored lowest among six domains, indicating weak risk framing and escalation guidance.
links.quote: Across models, empathy and stigma-free communication scored highest, whereas actionability and risk management scored lowest.

screen.reason: Evaluates the quality, safety, and bilingual performance of several LLM models generating patient communication for psychodermatology scenarios using expert clinician raters, without testing a specific deployment safeguard or operational intervention.
